audit_findings.title: Maintenance-capex treatment may materially overstate owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $48.725 million of 2025 construction spending, equal to 272.2% of the $17.9 million OE anchor; misclassified maintenance amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring replacement, compliance, or capacity-preservation expenditure omitted from maintenance capex directly overstates anchor OE and every scenario value.
audit_findings.evidence: During 2025, the Company invested $48,725 in construction expenditures for main extensions and an upgrade to the enterprise software system, as well as various replacements and improvements to infrastructure and routine items.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large mixed capital program but does not demonstrate that the OE workpaper classified it incorrectly. The issue is nevertheless material because even a modest unidentified maintenance portion could be large relative to the $17.9 million anchor.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the project-level 2025 capex classification, identify expenditures required to preserve existing service and regulatory compliance, deduct them from OE, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may be assigned to a fixed share base despite planned equity financing
audit_findings.magnitude: The April 2026 offering issued 1.750 million shares; the 16.263235 million valuation denominator already exceeds the 16.228581 million shares outstanding on August 6, 2026 by 34,654 shares, or 0.21%; future financing dilution is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Future stock issuance increases the per-share denominator, while debt financing increases interest expense retained in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company plans to finance ongoing capital expenditures with internally-generated funds, borrowings against the Company’s line of credit, proceeds from the issuance of common stock under its dividend reinvestment and direct stock purchase and sale plan and ESPP, potential common stock or debt issues and customer advances and contributions.
audit_findings.explanation: The known 2026 equity financing is substantially reflected in the supplied share count, so the record does not show a current denominator error. Additional financing relates to future capital programs and could reduce per-share value if forecast growth includes the benefits without the associated dilution or interest cost.
audit_findings.action: For each forecast year, reconcile capital expenditures and internally generated funds to planned debt and equity funding; update interest expense, issued shares, and contributed capital consistently before calculating per-share value.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 tax benefit may not represent sustainable owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.924 million filed 2025 ongoing TPR net income-tax benefit, equal to 21.9% of the $17.9 million OE anchor; sustainable adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An unusually low or negative tax burden increases after-tax anchor OE and propagates through all forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects the level to be lower in 2026, increasing the effective tax rate as compared to 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that TPR deductions materially benefited 2025 earnings, but it does not establish that the anchor failed to normalize them or that the benefit will disappear. Materiality is open because the filed benefit is large relative to OE. The $0.679 million tax benefit and negative 5.8% effective rate reported for the first half of 2026 show that favorable taxation persisted at least through June 2026, while management still expected the rate to rise later.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the anchor tax adjustment, estimate sustainable cash taxes using expected eligible TPR deductions and regulatory flow-through, and rerun the valuation with normalized after-tax OE.

audit_findings.title: Known 2026 rate relief is not visible in the smooth growth assumptions
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.850 million authorized annual revenue increase, equal to 105.3% of the $17.9 million OE anchor; first-half 2026 revenue increased $5.934 million and operating income increased $2.792 million year over year; net OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The rate order creates a revenue step-change above the FY2025 anchor that should enter forecast OE after deducting the DSIC reset, incremental expenses, taxes, and financing costs.
audit_findings.evidence: Effective March 1, 2026, the PPUC authorized an increase in water rates designed to produce approximately $ 16,000 in additional annual revenues and an increase in wastewater rates designed to produce approximately $ 2,850 in additional annual revenues.
audit_findings.explanation: This is more than a hypothetical risk: the rate increase took effect March 1, 2026 and the June quarter shows substantial realized revenue and operating-income growth. Smooth growth of only negative 1% to positive 5% from FY2025 can therefore understate near-term OE unless the step-change was incorporated separately. The gross authorization cannot be treated entirely as OE.
audit_findings.action: Build a 2026 run-rate from reported year-to-date results, isolate rate realization and the DSIC reset, deduct incremental operating costs, taxes, and financing effects, and rerun every scenario from the revised OE path.

audit_findings.title: Non-cash AFUDC may remain in the OE numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: At most $0.820 million of filed 2025 AFUDC, equal to 4.6% of the $17.9 million anchor; if fully included, approximately $11.5 million or $0.71 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unremoved AFUDC increases earnings-based OE despite producing no current cash, thereby increasing forecast operating value and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: These costs are reflected as non-cash income during the construction period and as an addition to the cost of plant constructed.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not establish whether AFUDC was removed. Even if the entire filed 2025 amount remained in the anchor, the computed base-value effect is about $0.71 per share, which is small relative to the $18.55 gap between the $15.50 base value and the $34.05 market price and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that both debt and equity AFUDC were removed without a duplicative capex adjustment; rerun the anchor if the workpaper shows otherwise.

audit_findings.title: Refundable customer advances are an economic claim outside interest expense
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.953 million outstanding at June 30, 2026, equal to 11.1% of the $252 million base equity value or $1.72 per valuation share; repayments were $0.716 million in 2025 and $0.621 million in first-half 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected refunds are owner cash outflows outside interest expense; alternatively, any enforceable residual claim may require a bridge deduction, subject to avoiding double counting customer-financed plant excluded from rate base.
audit_findings.evidence: Customer advances are cash payments from developers, municipalities, customers, or builders for construction of utility plant, and are refundable upon completion of construction, as operating revenues are earned.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and recurring refunds are demonstrated, but the record does not establish that the full balance should be deducted or how much will become nonrefundable contributions. Its scale relative to base equity value makes the unresolved treatment reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an advance-by-project runoff schedule, estimate refunds versus transfers to contributions, reconcile customer-funded plant and rate-base exclusions, and rerun OE for expected refunds or the bridge for any remaining claim without double counting.
